fi-paracheirodon-axelrodi.title: Cardinal Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-axelrodi.summary: A brilliant red-and-blue schooling tetra for warm, soft-water community and planted tanks.
rows: Schooling. Keep a group of at least 8–10
Quality flakes or micro-pellets plus live or frozen bloodworm, daphnia and similar small foods
Easy for farm-bred fish. Wild fish are less forgiving of poor water
Rio Negro and Orinoco basins (Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela). Most are now farm-bred
notes: Looks best in a planted tank with fairly dim light, driftwood and some floating plants.
Good tankmates: other small tetras, pencilfish, hatchetfish, small catfish and peaceful dwarf cichlids.

fi-poecilia-reticulata.title: Guppy
fi-poecilia-reticulata.summary: The guppy, Poecilia reticulata, is a livebearer native to northeastern South America and the southern Caribbean, including Venezuela and Trinidad. One of the most popular aquarium fish in the world,…
rows: Wild fish are primarily insectivorous, but today's tank-bred fish are far-removed from their ancestors and will accept most foods offered.
Native to northeastern South America and the southern Caribbean with its original range considered to cover Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana plus the islands of…
notes: Unfussy, though a planted tank with floating vegetation is appreciated.

fi-paracheirodon-innesi.title: Neon Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-innesi.summary: The neon tetra, Paracheirodon innesi, is a small characid from the Amazon basin in Colombia, Brazil and Peru, found in acidic forest streams. Years of commercial breeding have weakened the ornamental…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
The type locality was originally given as 'near Iquitos', referring to the city of that name in the rainforest of Loreto region, Peru, although the specimens themselves derived…
notes: Provided healthy stock can be obtained (see 'Notes') maintenance presents few problems although it perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-puntius-titteya.title: Cherry Barb
fi-puntius-titteya.summary: The cherry barb, Puntius titteya, is a small cyprinid endemic to the Kelani and Nilwala river basins in the southwestern 'wet zone' of Sri Lanka. Among the most ubiquitous small cyprinids in the…
rows: schooling species by nature, and at least 6-10 specimens should be purchased.
Wild fish are probably foragers feeding on diatoms, algae, organic detritus, small insects, worms, crustaceans, and other zooplankton.
Endemic to Sri Lanka where it is restricted to the Kelani and Nilwala river basins in the southwestern 'wet zone' of the island, plus smaller drainages in the area between them.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants, driftwood roots or branches, and leaf litter also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

in-neocaridina-davidi.title: Neocaridina Dwarf Shrimp
in-neocaridina-davidi.summary: Colorful dwarf shrimp that breed in freshwater. Excellent clean-up crew for planted tanks when fish will not eat the shrimplets.
rows: Females to about 1.5 in (4 cm); males smaller
Nanos work; 10 gal+ is better for breeding. Sponge-filter or prefilter the intake
Peaceful; almost any fish will eat babies
Biofilm, algae, leftover foods, blanched veg, calcium-rich shrimp foods
About 6.5–8.5 with enough GH/KH for clean molts
China and Taiwan; ornamental morphs are captive-bred
notes: Mixing colors yields mixed offspring.
A clear split shell is usually a molt, not a corpse.

in-nerite-snail.title: Nerite Snail
in-nerite-snail.sci: Neritidae (trade includes Vittina waigiensis / red racer, zebra, horned, olive, etc.)
in-nerite-snail.summary: Popular algae-eating snails that clean glass and hardscape without overrunning a freshwater tank.
rows: About dime-to-quarter size depending on type (roughly 0.5–1.5 in)
Works in 10 gal+ community tanks; nanos OK if not overstocked. Tight lid required
Peaceful; avoid loaches, crayfish, goldfish and cichlids that may eat them
Algae browser / scavenger. Soft film, green and brown algae, diatoms, leftover food; supplement if the tank is too clean
Alkaline preferred (~7.5); harder water and calcium help shells
Coastal and brackish-associated waters; freshwater aquarium strains are widely farmed/collected for the trade
notes: White hard egg capsules appear in freshwater but rarely hatch without brackish rearing.
Place snails upright — many struggle to flip themselves over.

fi-aphyocharax-paraguayensis.title: Panda Tetra
fi-aphyocharax-paraguayensis.summary: The dawn tetra, Aphyocharax nattereri, is a small characid from southern Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay. In the hobby it is usually called A. paraguayensis, a name considered a synonym of A. nattereri…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. Unfussy and will accept most dried, frozen and live foods.
notes: Looks most at home in a planted aquarium.
Provide areas of dense vegetation, along with some open areas for swimming.

fi-aphyocharax-rathbuni.title: Green Fire Tetra
fi-aphyocharax-rathbuni.summary: The green fire tetra, or Rathbun's bloodfin, Aphyocharax rathbuni, is a characid endemic to the Paraguay, Paraná and Uruguay river drainages. It is found in Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay,…
rows: Not a fussy eater in captivity and will accept most aquarium foods.
Endemic to the Paraguay, Paraná and Uruguay river drainages in Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay.
notes: A well planted aquarium with sandy substrate is recommended.
This can be decorated with bogwood, roots and pebbles.

fi-carinotetraodon-travancoricus.title: Dwarf Freshwater BB Puffer
fi-carinotetraodon-travancoricus.summary: The dwarf puffer, Carinotetraodon travancoricus, is a tiny freshwater puffer endemic to the state of Kerala in southern India. Also known as the Malabar puffer and probably the smallest species of…
rows: As is the case with with most puffers, this species relishes all kinds of shellfish, as well as worms and other live and frozen foods.
Endemic to the state of Kerala, India.
notes: This species fares best in a heavily-planted setup, perhaps further decorated with twisted roots and branches to provide additional cover.
This type of set-up will provide plenty of broken lines of sight (important to reduce aggression between individuals) and a varied habitat for these inquisitive fish to explore.

fi-colisa-chuna.title: Red Honey Gourami
fi-colisa-chuna.summary: The honey gourami, Trichogaster chuna, is a labyrinth fish from the Ganges and Brahmaputra systems of India and Bangladesh, with records from Nepal. Virtually all fish on sale are commercially…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates

schooling fishes it does seem to require interaction with conspecifics and displays more interesting behaviour when maintained in numbers, meaning the purchase of no less than 4-6 specimens is recommended.
Likely to prey on insects and other small invertebrates in nature.
Known from the Ganges River in northern India, including its floodplain and delta in Bangladesh, plus the Brahmaputra system in the states of Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, and…
notes: Fares best in a well-planted, shady set-up with plenty of surface cover in the form of tall stem or floating plants.
Driftwood can also be used and other plants such as Microsorum or Taxiphyllum spp.

fi-corydoras-pygmaeus.title: Pygmy Corydoras
fi-corydoras-pygmaeus.summary: The pygmy cory, Gastrodermus pygmaeus, long known as Corydoras pygmaeus, is one of a handful of tiny Corydoras species and appears to be endemic to the Rio Madeira basin, Brazil. Unlike most of its…
rows: groups in nature so it's best to buy at least 6, preferably 10 or more.
Any food offered must be small enough for its tiny mouth.
Appears to be endemic to the Rio Madeira basin, Brazil.
notes: It looks superb in a heavily planted setup decorated with pieces of bogwood and twisted roots, perhaps with a layer of surface vegetation to dim the lighting a touch.

fi-danio-choprae.title: Glolite Danio
fi-danio-choprae.summary: The glowlight danio, Danio choprae, is a small cyprinid from northern Myanmar, apparently restricted to the Mogaung Chaung system. Available in the trade since around 2003, it quickly became one of…
rows: schooling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens which will develop a pecking order among themselves.
Almost certain to prey chiefly on insects and their larvae in nature.
The type specimens were collected from 'small rocky streams' of the Mogaung Chaung river system close to the towns of 'Kamaing' (often referred to as Kar Maing) and Namma…
notes: Looks particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement with a darker substrate, and may appear paler in sparsely-decorated set-ups.
We suggest maintaining it in a well-planted aquarium or set-up designed to resemble a flowing river or stream, with a substrate of variably-sized rocks and gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-danio-erythromicron.title: Dwarf Emerald Rasbora
fi-danio-erythromicron.summary: Danio erythromicron is a miniature danionin from Lake Inle and its surrounding watershed in Shan State, eastern Myanmar. Fully grown at just 20 mm, it is sold under trade names including 'emerald…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Likely to feed on small invertebrates, algae and other zooplankton in nature.
Known from the isolated mountain lake of Inlé and surrounding watershed in Shan state, eastern Myanmar, and also occurs close to Loi Kaw township in neighbouring Kayah state to the south.
notes: This timid species should ideally be kept in a heavily-planted set-up, preferably with a dark substrate.
The broken lines of sight that exist in such a display allow it to display natural behaviour as well as helping to reduce skittishness.

fi-danio-margaritatus.title: Celestial Pearl Danio
fi-danio-margaritatus.summary: The celestial pearl danio, Danio margaritatus, is a miniature cyprinid from the Salween drainage in Shan State, eastern Myanmar. First marketed as 'Galaxy Rasbora' after its discovery in 2006, it…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Likely to feed on small invertebrates, algae and other zooplankton in nature.
Type locality is 'Pools at foot of mountain near Hopong town 30 kilometers east of Taunggyi, Myanmar, elevation 1040 meters', thought restricted to a single locality around 1,040…
notes: This timid species should ideally be kept in a heavily-planted set-up, preferably with a dark substrate.
The broken lines of sight that exist in such a display allow it to display natural behaviour as well as helping to reduce skittishness.

fi-danio-tinwini.title: Gold Ring Tinwini Danio
fi-danio-tinwini.summary: The gold ring danio, Danio tinwini, is a tiny cyprinid from the Mogaung Chaung, an Irrawaddy tributary in Kachin State, northern Myanmar. Seen in the trade since 2003, it has been sold as 'Danio sp.…
rows: schooling species by nature and should be maintained in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Almost certain to prey chiefly on insects and their larvae in nature as with most danionins.
To date it's known only from the Mogaung Chaung (Mogaung stream), Myitkyina District, Kachin State, northern Myanmar, the same watershed to which D.
notes: Looks particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement with a darker substrate, and may appear paler in sparsely-decorated set-ups.
We suggest maintaining it in a well-planted aquarium or set-up designed to resemble a flowing river or stream, with a substrate of variably-sized rocks and gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-hyphessobrycon-amandae.title: Ember Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-amandae.summary: The ember tetra, Hyphessobrycon amandae, is a tiny characid from the rio das Mortes, a tributary of the Araguaia in Mato Grosso, Brazil. Also traded as the 'Amanda's', 'dwarf red', 'red' and 'fire'…
rows: schools meaning a minimum of 8-10 specimens is the recommended purchase since the fish will be less shy and display more interesting behaviour.
Predator / carnivore. Probably a micropredator feeding on tiny invertebrates and other zooplankton in nature.
Type locality is 'Rio das Mortes, some 100 km before its confluence with the Braço Maior of the Rio Araguaia (the western border of the Isla do Bananal).
notes: Should ideally be kept in a heavily-planted set-up, preferably with a dark substrate.
Floating plants are a useful addition as are driftwood branches and dried leaf litter, the latter in particular driving establishment of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-iriatherina-werneri.title: Threadfin Rainbow
fi-iriatherina-werneri.summary: The threadfin rainbowfish, Iriatherina werneri, is a small rainbowfish from southern New Guinea, Cape York in Queensland and the Northern Territory. Although widely traded and produced on a…
rows: shoaling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 6 specimens, ideally 10 or more.
Feeds on floating or suspended phytoplankton, diatoms, and other zooplankton in nature, and in the aquarium must be offered items of a suitable size for its tiny mouth.
Described from 'Merauke, Irian Jaya, Indonesia ' which corresponds to modern day Merauke Regency, Papua province, Indonesia, on the island of New Guinea.
notes: Best kept in a densely-planted tank and an excellent choice for the carefully-aquascaped set-up.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-nannostomus-beckfordi.title: Red Beckfords Pencilfish
fi-nannostomus-beckfordi.summary: The golden pencilfish, Nannostomus beckfordi, is a lebiasinid widely distributed across Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana, Brazil and Venezuela. The type species of the genus and fairly ubiquitous in…
rows: Predator / carnivore. A micropredator feeding on tiny invertebrates and other zooplankton in nature.
Type locality is 'Goedverwagting, a plantation on the Coast of Demerara, Guyana ' but this species is widely-distributed throughout rivers of Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana…
notes: Should ideally be kept in a heavily-planted set-up, preferably with a dark substrate.
The broken lines of sight that exist in such a display allow it to display natural behaviour as well as helping to reduce skittishness.

fi-oryzias-woworae.title: Daisy Ricefish Killie
fi-oryzias-woworae.summary: Daisy's ricefish, Oryzias woworae, is known only from a single stream on the island of Muna, Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia. At 25-30 mm it is the most diminutive Oryzias known from Sulawesi. It…
rows: Omnivore. Unfussy but must be provided with foods of a suitable size.
Described and known only from a single locality, a stream named Mata air Fotuno, in Parigi district on the island of Muna, South East Sulawesi (Sulawesi Tenggara) province,…
notes: Has proven to be adaptable with no special requirements in terms of décor though it tends to be less colurful when maintained in a sparsely-decorated set-up.
It arguably looks best in a display inspired by its natural habitat which could consist of a sandy substrate, some water-worn tree roots and branches plus a few handfuls of leaf litter.

fi-pethia-gelius.title: Dwarf Golden Barb
fi-pethia-gelius.summary: The golden dwarf barb, Pethia gelius, is a small cyprinid native to the Ganges and Brahmaputra river drainages of northern India and Bangladesh. Records suggest a wider range, including Tamil Nadu…
rows: schooling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Predator / carnivore. Naturally a micropredator feeding on small insects, worms, crustaceans and other zooplankton in nature.
Described from 'Ponds and ditches of northeastern Bengal', and generally considered native to the Ganges and Brahmaputra river drainages in northern India, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
notes: Best kept in a densely-planted tank and is an excellent choice for the carefully-aquascaped set-up.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-pseudomugil-furcatus.title: Furcata Rainbow
fi-pseudomugil-furcatus.summary: The forktail blue-eye, Pseudomugil furcatus, is a small pseudomugilid endemic to the Northern and Milne Bay provinces of eastern Papua New Guinea. Aquarium stock is bred commercially and apparently…
rows: shoaling species and should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Feeds chiefly on floating or suspended zooplankton, phytoplankton, and invertebrates in nature, and in the aquarium must be offered items of a suitable size.
Described from 'Peria Creek, Kwagira River, eastern Papua New Guinea ' and despite its popularity in the aquarium hobby is endemic to a relatively small area in the country's…
notes: Best kept in a densely-planted tank and an excellent choice for the carefully-aquascaped set-up.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-rhinogobius-duospilus.title: Rainbow Goby
fi-rhinogobius-duospilus.summary: The white-cheeked goby, Rhinogobius duospilus, is a small goby from Hong Kong and southern China, living in clear hill streams. It was often sold in the past as 'Rhinogobius wui', a name now listed…
rows: In nature it feeds on small invertebrates.
Described from Hong Kong and known from much of southern China, including Shenzhen in Guangdong province immediately north of the type locality.
notes: Not difficult to maintain under the correct conditions; we strongly recommend keeping it in a tank designed to simulate a flowing stream with a substrate of variably-sized rocks, sand, fine gravel, and some water-worn boulders.
This can be further furnished with driftwood branches, terracotta pipes, plant pots, etc., arranged to form a network of nooks, crannies, and shaded spots, thus providing broken lines of sight.

fi-sphaerichthys-vaillanti.title: Samurai Gourami
fi-sphaerichthys-vaillanti.summary: Vaillant's chocolate gourami, Sphaerichthys vaillanti, is a labyrinth fish that appears to be endemic to the Kapuas drainage in Indonesian Borneo. It is also traded as the 'samurai gourami', a…
rows: schooling/shoaling fishes it does seem to require interaction with conspecifics and displays more interesting behaviour when maintained in numbers, meaning we recommend the purchase of no less than 6 individuals.
Predator / carnivore. Primarily a micropredator feeding on small aquatic crustaceans, worms, insect larvae and other zooplankton.
Type locality is the village of Nangah Sebroeang which lies south of the Danau Sentarum National Park within the upper Kapuas river basin, West Kalimantan (Kalimantan Barat)…
notes: Provided adequate cover and structure is available this species is unfussy with regards to décor with ceramic flowerpots, lengths of plastic piping and other artificial materials all useful additions.
A more natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots and caves are formed.

fi-macrotocinclus-affinis.title: Otocinclus
fi-macrotocinclus-affinis.summary: Otocinclus affinis, the golden otocinclus, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Loricariidae, the suckermouth armored catfishes, and the subfamily Hypoptopomatinae,…
rows: Up to about 5.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-stiphodon-elegans.title: Elegant Stiphodon Goby Male
fi-stiphodon-elegans.summary: Stiphodon elegans, commonly known as the Green Riffle Goby, is a species of freshwater goby. They can live from 3–8 years, but they still remain small throughout their lifespans, only growing to up…
rows: Up to about 5.2 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-enteromius-fasciolatus.title: Blue Barred Barb (African Banded Barb)
fi-enteromius-fasciolatus.summary: A small African barb with 10–15 blue-black vertical bars, long sold as Barbus barilioides (now an old synonym). It comes from slow, heavily planted, often tea-stained waters and colors up best in soft water under dim light.
rows: Up to about 2.4 in (60 mm SL)
30 × 12 in footprint (about 18 gal) or larger for a group
Generally peaceful; males keep a pecking order
Shoal of 8 or more, with plenty of cover and broken sight lines
Omnivore. Flake or pellets plus small live or frozen foods (brine shrimp, Daphnia, bloodworm) and some vegetable matter
Central-southern Africa: Cunene, Okavango, upper and middle Zambezi (incl. Kafue and Lake Kariba), upper Kasai and the Luapula/Bangweulu area of the upper Congo
notes: Old name: Barbus (Barbodes) barilioides. FishBase now places it in Enteromius; Seriously Fish still writes 'Barbus' fasciolatus.
Likes a sandy bottom, wood, leaf litter and floating plants; keep the flow gentle. It can be delicate right after import, so add it to an established tank.

fi-trichopsis-pumila.title: Sparkling Gourami (Pygmy Gourami)
fi-trichopsis-pumila.summary: A tiny labyrinth fish from the lower Mekong and Thailand that sparkles red, green and blue. Both sexes make audible croaking sounds, and most sold are farm-bred.
rows: Peaceful and easily bullied; may eat baby shrimp
A pair or small group, alone or with very small peaceful fish
Takes dried foods once settled, but needs plenty of small live or frozen foods (Daphnia, brine shrimp, bloodworm) for best color
Lower Mekong basin (Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand) and central and southern Thailand; slow, plant-choked waters
notes: Best in a heavily planted, shady tank with floating plants or tall stems for surface cover; keep the flow gentle (an air-driven sponge filter is enough).
Good tankmates: small rasboras such as Boraras and Trigonostigma, and small loaches like Pangio.

fi-dario-dario.title: Scarlet Badis
fi-dario-dario.summary: One of the smallest perch-like fish, from Brahmaputra tributaries in north-east India. Males are bright red with blue bars. Shy and slow, it suits small, calm planted tanks.
rows: Under 1 in: about 0.8 in (20 mm) SL; females smaller
Retiring and easily outcompeted; males fight each other in small tanks
One male with one or more females in small tanks; a group only with room for each male to hold a territory
Micropredator: needs small live or frozen foods (baby brine shrimp, Daphnia, grindal or micro worms). Skip bloodworm and Tubifex, which can lead to obesity and disease
Tributaries of the Brahmaputra in West Bengal and Assam, India (possibly Bhutan)
notes: Dense cover, a soft substrate, plants such as Cryptocoryne and moss, and only very small, calm tankmates (or none).
